sources.news_title: Israel PM hails Indian pilot for averting disaster
sources.text:
Israel's leader credited the Indian pilot of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, as well as the aircraft's passengers, with averting catastrophe on Wednesday after the man was attacked by his co-pilot, sparking a fight for control of the aircraft and forcing an emergency landing.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the co-pilot of the flydubai jet had been trying to crash it and kill all its passengers, with Israel's foreign ministry denouncing the incident as "an attempted terrorist attack" aimed at damaging the country's relationship with one of its key Middle Eastern partners.
Passengers gave a similar account of the incident, describing rushing the cockpit after the plane suddenly plummeted, losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.
Flydubai said all the passengers – of whom 166 out of 174 were Israeli, according to media reports – were safe, adding that the reasons for the altercation were unknown.
AFPTV images later showed another flydubai plane carrying the passengers touch down at Tel Aviv airport, hours after their initial flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia's Tabuk.
"During the flight, as they approached the country, one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot, and apparently tried to crash the plane with everyone on board," Netanyahu said in a video message.
"I salute these heroes," he said of the passengers, adding "they prevented a major disaster."
He later hailed the pilot who was wounded – identified as Indian national Smit Machchhar – "for his extraordinary bravery," praising him for fighting back despite being wounded and "preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster."
The Indian embassy said Machchhar was being treated at a Saudi hospital, while the company operating the airport in Tabuk said the co-pilot was also found to be injured upon landing.
Footage shared by the premier's office on Wednesday evening showed Netanyahu meeting the passengers of the flight at Tel Aviv airport and embracing a man in a bloodied shirt.
"Is that from him (the assailant)?" the premier asks, pointing at the stains, as the man replies in the affirmative.
Passenger Miryam Shira Ohayon said the plane was "pretty much out of control" as the incident unfolded over Jordan.
"So the co-pilot tried to murder the pilot and basically carry out a suicide attack on the plane," she told reporters by speaker-phone held up by her mother, who was waiting at Ben Gurion Airport.
"It was really on the way to crashing, and it was simply the resourcefulness of many people who took control of the co-pilot and neutralised him," she said.
The airline later said it was another "on-duty flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely."
It also announced it was suspending flights to Israel while the incident was being investigated.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz described the incident as "an attempted jihadist terror attack," but did not identify his source for assigning a motive.
The director general of Israel's foreign ministry called it "an attempted terrorist attack against Israelis, the United Arab Emirates, and the Abraham Accords," referring to the peace deal signed by the two countries in 2020.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said he had spoken with top UAE diplomat Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, with the pair agreeing "to collaborate against extremist elements seeking to harm security and undermine stability."
Describing the flight's sudden plunge, passenger Almog Italie said it was like "we were having very big turbulence" before fighting erupted near the cockpit.
"The other passengers from the front took over control," he said via video call from Saudi Arabia.
"It has been a long day, luckily for us it's ended," Italie said hours later after landing in Tel Aviv.
Fellow passenger Chaim Nazarovitz said the ordeal had been "very terrifying," adding that for a moment he felt like he was "not among the living."
Israel's Kan public broadcaster and Channel 12 reported that the Israeli military had scrambled fighter jets after fears of a possible hijacking.
In a video from inside the plane, one passenger – blood dripping from an open wound on his head – pleaded for assistance and said they were descending into Saudi Arabia.
Israel has no formal ties with the Gulf kingdom, but Italie said the group received a "very warm" welcome there.
The incident comes months into a regional war that erupted in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
It also comes just ahead of Israeli elections due to be held at the end of October.
On Tuesday, Netanyahu said there were "indications" that Israel's enemies could try to attack ahead of elections, and was accused of "fear-mongering" by the opposition chief. (AFP)
Edited by Robert Kemp

sources.news_title: Netanyahu says one flydubai pilot wanted to crash plane, 'major disaster' averted
sources.text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Wednesday that one of the pilots of a flydubai plane bound for Tel Aviv had planned to crash it and kill its mostly Israeli passengers, who stopped a "major disaster".
"During the flight, as they approached the country, one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot, and apparently tried to crash the plane with everyone on board," Netanyahu said in a video message, calling the passengers "heroes" who "prevented a major disaster".
He added that Saudi Arabia has arrested and is interrogating a flydubai co-pilot.
This came after the involved flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was forced to be diverted to Saudi Arabia where it landed safely, three Israeli officials said. Both pilots were found to be wounded on landing in Saudi Arabia.
In the first comment by an official, Israel's far-right national security minister Itamar Ben Gvir alleged an attempted "terrorist" attack in the incident, in which none of the passengers reported injuries.
The flydubai plane was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia's Tabuk "at 9:45 am (0645 GMT) and its captain and copilot were found to have injuries and were transported to hospital", a statement from the company operating the airport said.
The low-cost carrier had earlier said flight FZ 1073 "experienced an incident while en route. The aircraft has landed safely in Tabuk Airport (TUU) and all passengers are safe and accounted for".
According to data from the Flightradar website, the aircraft suddenly lost altitude during the flight, dropping from nearly 34,000 feet at 0521 GMT to less than 17,000 feet at 0522 GMT.
Passenger Miryam Shira Ohayon said the plane was "pretty much out of control" when one of the pilots tried to stab the other while they were flying over Jordan en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
"So the co-pilot tried to murder the pilot and basically carry out a suicide attack on the plane," she told reporters by speakerphone held up by her mother who was waiting at Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv.
"It was really on the way to crashing, and it was simply the resourcefulness of many people who took control of the co-pilot and neutralized him," she said.
"There was also a doctor who gave first aid, and people who treated both of them. Other than the pilot, there were no injuries, but the bigger fear was really a crash, which is exactly what he was trying to do."
Several Israeli media reported that a fight had broken out between the plane's pilots, reportedly causing a distress signal to be activated.
Israeli media also reported that two other pilots were flying on the plane as passengers, and that they had taken over the controls to carry out the emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
At Ben Gurion airport, families gathered to await the return of their loved ones.
Earlier, Yasmin Abukasis, Ohayon's mother, told AFP her daughter called her from Saudi Arabia: "She said one pilot tried to kill the other pilot with a knife. They heard shouting".
Another passenger went to the cockpit "and saw a lot of blood. She started screaming 'come help' and some people went in and caught the guy", she added.
- 'Going down very fast' -
"All the while, the plane started going down very fast. People thought they were going to die."
She added that two other pilots in the back later took over the controls.
Neither the airline nor authorities of the countries involved provided details on what happened on board or on the pilots' nationalities, but some Israeli media said one was Omani and the other Emirati.
Israel's Kan public broadcaster and Channel 12 reported that the Israeli military had scrambled fighter jets after fears of a possible hijacking.
The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the premier had held consultations on the matter and was "monitoring developments".
Contacted by AFP, the Israeli military said it was "checking" the reports.
Meir Zohar, the father of passenger Ido Zohar, told AFP his son had told him by text message that he was well, but that he had no other news.
"We heard on the news what happened in the sky of Abu Dhabi," he said.
"He told us that everything is okay, he didn't tell me that much."
- Bloodied T-shirt -
Israeli media, citing anonymous sources, reported that the passengers on board had stepped in to separate the two pilots during their altercation, publishing photos of a passenger with a bloodied T-shirt.
Channel 12 reported that authorities were investigating whether or not one of the pilots had attempted a possible suicide by trying to crash the plane, with the other pilot apparently intervening to prevent the crash.
An AFP correspondent in Tabuk, where the plane landed, saw heavy security near the airport, with several police vehicles and an ambulance parked at the terminal.
Access to the terminal remained open.
In photos sent to AFP by one of the passengers, travellers, including children, are seen gathered in an airport lounge, with some sitting on the floor, while one man is wearing a white T-shirt and jeans stained with blood.
The incident comes as tensions are high across the Middle East, amid the regional war that erupted in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
It also comes just ahead of close-fought Israeli elections due to be held at the end of October.
On Tuesday, Netanyahu said there were "indications" that Israel's enemies could try to attack ahead of elections, and was accused of "fear-mongering" by the opposition chief.
(AFP and Reuters)

sources.news_title: Terror in the Cockpit: Israel’s New Aviation Nightmare
sources.text:
What happened aboard Flydubai Flight FZ1073 on Wednesday should send shockwaves through Israel’s security establishment.
The Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight was carrying Israelis when, according to Israeli authorities and passenger accounts, the co-pilot repeatedly stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar inside the cockpit and apparently attempted to seize control of the aircraft. Israeli authorities subsequently announced they were treating the incident as a terrorist attack.
Flight data showed the Boeing 737 plunging from approximately 34,000 feet to 14,000 feet during the crisis. Israeli fighter jets were scrambled, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz held urgent consultations. The aircraft eventually landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
But this story could have ended very differently.
Captain Machchhar, an Indian pilot with roughly 15 years of commercial aviation experience, reportedly fought back despite being seriously wounded. Passengers and crew breached the cockpit and subdued the attacker, while two additional pilots traveling aboard the aircraft were able to assume control. Netanyahu later praised Machchhar’s bravery, saying his actions helped save 174 lives.
The immediate disaster was prevented. The strategic questions are only beginning.
Arab affairs analyst Zvi Yehezkeli raised the possibility that this was not simply the action of one radicalized individual. He argued that recruiting someone with access to an airliner carrying Israelis could indicate sophisticated planning, potentially involving a state actor such as Iran or one of its proxies. That remains an assessment—not an established finding—and Israeli officials have not publicly confirmed Iranian involvement.
But the vulnerability exposed by the incident is real.
Israel revolutionized aviation security after the wave of airline hijackings and attacks of the 1960s and 1970s. Israeli passengers became among the most heavily protected travelers in the world.
Yet the security architecture was primarily designed around keeping terrorists out of the cockpit.
What happens when the potential terrorist is already inside?
That question becomes especially serious as Israelis increasingly travel aboard foreign airlines whose pilots and crews are vetted under security systems Israel does not control.
Wednesday’s incident may therefore represent more than an extraordinary act of heroism aboard one aircraft.
It may have exposed the next battlefield in Israel’s continuing struggle against terrorism: the trusted insiders who already possess access to the systems they could potentially turn into weapons.
Israel survived this attempt.
Now it must learn from it.

sources.news_title: Netanyahu identifies and praises stabbed pilot as a ‘true hero’
sources.text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has identified the stabbed pilot on the Flydubai flight as Smit Machchhar from India.
Netanyahu praised the captain as a “true hero,” saying he demonstrated “extraordinary bravery” and saved the lives of 174 people.

“Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster,” he said on X.
The India Embassy in Saudi Arabia described Machchhar as “brave” and wished him a speedy recovery. He is being treated at a hospital in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
“A full update on his health is awaited but he is reported to be in stable condition,” the embassy said in a statement. “We hope that he recovers from his injuries at the earliest. We are in touch with his family and assure them that we will continue to follow up on his health with Saudi authorities and extend all possible assistance for his wellbeing.
The co-pilot of a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv tried to crash the plane after stabbing Machchhar but passengers subdued him while other pilots landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia, Israeli officials say.
Describing the event as “a highly severe security incident,” Netanyahu said Saudi authorities would interrogate the co-pilot of Flydubai flight FZ1073 from the United Arab Emirates to Israel.
The airline said in a statement that the underlying reasons for the event remained unknown and warned against “premature speculation”.
The cause of the altercation between the pilots was not clear.
The co-pilot, who an Israeli official identified as an Omani citizen, was arrested after the plane landed, Netanyahu said.
Israel’s transport ministry said there would be a joint investigation of the incident with the defence establishment.
“All passengers are out of harm’s way,” Netanyahu said in a video statement released by his office.
He also ordered tighter security on both Israeli and non-Israeli carriers flying into Israel.
The passengers departed Saudi Arabia for Israel aboard a Flydubai replacement aircraft after eight hours on the ground.
The FlyDubai replacement plane later landed in Israel.
Netanyahu quoted a passenger as saying that passengers along with a member of the crew broke into the cockpit after the aircraft “entered a tailspin and began to dive” and found the co-pilot “trying to sabotage the plane’s systems”.
“They saved many lives. They prevented a heavy disaster,” he said.
A second set of pilots on board, who were due to replace the first pair, landed the plane.
The aircraft’s flight data showed it suddenly and rapidly descended by nearly 14,000ft (around 4000m) in less than 30 seconds before a first emergency signal was sent on Wednesday morning, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24.
Yasmin Abukasis said her daughter Miriam, who was among the passengers on the flight, had told her that she had heard screaming and that a man holding a knife had forced one of the pilots onto the floor, and that there was blood everywhere.
Israeli media published a photo purportedly taken from inside the plane, which appeared to show a passenger’s blood-soaked shirt.
Flydubai operates daily return flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv, a route that is popular among Israelis.
Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk airport, where the plane landed, said both pilots had been hospitalised after sustaining injuries.

flydubai suspends all flights to and from Israel following FZ1073 cockpit incident
The airline announced the temporary suspension in coordination with relevant authorities while investigations continue. Affected passengers are being offered alternative travel options
Dubai: Following the incident on flight FZ1073 yesterday, flydubai announced the temporary suspension of its flights to and from Israel, in coordination with the relevant authorities, until ongoing investigations are completed.
The carrier, in a statement attributed to a spokesperson, said the temporary suspension was to allow the relevant authorities to continue their investigation and verify all the facts and circumstances related to the incident.
flydubai confirmed that the safety of its passengers, crew members and operations remains its top priority, noting its full commitment to supporting the ongoing investigation and maintaining the highest standards of safety and security in all its operations across its network of destinations.

sources.news_title: Smit Machchhar Health Update: Flydubai Captain Undergoes Surgery in Saudi Hospital as World Hails Him 'Hero'
sources.text:
Indian Flydubai captain Smit Machchhar has undergone surgery at a hospital in Saudi Arabia and is now in stable condition after being stabbed during a dramatic cockpit incident aboard an Israel-bound flight, according to local reports.
Machchhar was injured after an altercation broke out between the pilots of Flydubai Flight FZ1073, which was flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv on Wednesday. The aircraft was forced to divert to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia after plunging thousands of feet and transmitting an emergency signal.
Reuters reported that Machchhar suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Both pilots were hospitalized in Tabuk following the incident.
Flydubai and Indian authorities are in contact with Machchhar's family, while the Indian government has said it is extending support to him and coordinating with the relevant authorities in Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
There has been no public indication that Machchhar has been discharged from the hospital.
What Happened to Smit Machchhar on Flydubai FZ1073?
The flight was traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv when a violent confrontation erupted in the cockpit. Israeli officials said the co-pilot, identified as an Omani national, stabbed Machchhar and then attempted to crash the aircraft. The aircraft reportedly plunged nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before passengers and crew intervened.
According to an account cited by Reuters, Machchhar was injured and lying on the cockpit floor when he managed to activate the release that opened the cockpit door. Passengers then entered the cockpit and helped overpower the other pilot. A second Flydubai crew member aboard the aircraft subsequently took control and landed the plane safely in Tabuk.
Passengers Hail Machchhar and Crew for Preventing Disaster
The incident has drawn widespread praise for the passengers and crew members who intervened during the emergency.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised passengers who entered the cockpit and restrained the co-pilot. Reuters reported that Netanyahu described one passenger involved in the intervention as a "hero."
According to the Reuters account, his ability to open the cockpit door allowed passengers to enter and intervene.
However, the full sequence of events remains under investigation, and Flydubai has said the underlying reasons for the incident are not yet known.
An Israeli passenger on a flydubai flight recounted the moment aboard the plane, saying that the co-pilot of the flight tried to crash the plane after stabbing the other pilot. He also mentioned that upon arriving in Saudi Arabia they were welcomed by the local authorities and were treated nicely before they boarded their plane to Israel.
Who Is Smit Machchhar?
Machchhar is an Indian national and has been a Flydubai captain since June 2022, according to his professional profile cited by Indian media. Before joining Flydubai, he spent about 11 years with SpiceJet in Mumbai, where he worked as a senior commander and later as a line training captain responsible for training and checking pilots.
His profile lists around 9,750 flying hours on Boeing 737 aircraft. Machchhar was reportedly the pilot in command of FZ1073 when the incident occurred.
Investigation Into Flydubai Cockpit Attack Continues
The motive behind the confrontation remains unclear. The co-pilot was taken into custody by Saudi authorities following the emergency landing and is expected to be questioned as part of the investigation. Reuters reported that Israel plans to tighten security checks on pilots flying into the country following the incident.
Flydubai has said it will issue further information after reviewing the cockpit voice recorder and other details surrounding the incident.

sources.text:
A routine flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv turned into a terrifying emergency.
A physical confrontation between the pilots reportedly sent the aircraft plunging thousands of feet. The aircraft then diverted to Saudi Arabia.
Israeli officials said the co-pilot is believed to have stabbed the captain in what they described as a possible attempted “terror attack”.
However, another Israeli official said the incident was not believed to be a hijacking, leaving key details still under investigation.
So what happened inside the cockpit?
Flight-tracking data showed the Boeing 737 dropped nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before emergency signals were transmitted.
Cockpit Incident Investigated
Flightradar24 later recorded a signal indicating possible unlawful interference.
Cabin crew reportedly entered the cockpit and took control as the aircraft diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely.
All passengers were accounted for, while both pilots were taken to hospital with injuries.
Reports from passengers described screams, a man holding a knife and blood inside the cockpit.
Reuters could not independently verify some of the claims or images circulating online.

For the passengers, the destination suddenly mattered less than one thing: getting safely back on the ground.

sources.news_title: Off-Duty Pilots Foil Alleged Plot to Crash Flydubai Flight, Saving 170 Israelis
sources.text:
Passengers and crew members subdued a flydubai co-pilot after he allegedly attacked and stabbed the captain during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, prompting an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, Israeli officials said Wednesday.
Flydubai flight FZ1073, carrying more than 170 passengers, including a large number of Israelis, was diverted to Tabuk after a violent confrontation in the cockpit. The aircraft made a safe landing after a second pair of pilots aboard the plane took control, according to Israeli officials and reports from passengers.
Flight-tracking data reviewed by Reuters showed the aircraft suddenly lost nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds. The rapid descent triggered emergency signals and heightened fears that the aircraft was in danger. Passengers and crew members then entered the cockpit and restrained the attacker, allowing the flight to continue safely toward Tabuk.
Both pilots were injured and were taken to hospital after the aircraft landed. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the co-pilot was arrested by Saudi authorities and described the incident as a serious security event. Israeli officials said the suspect was an Omani national. The motive remains unclear.
Flydubai confirmed that the flight diverted to Tabuk after an incident onboard and said all passengers were safe and accounted for. The airline said the underlying reasons for the incident remained unknown and cautioned against premature speculation while authorities investigate.
Passenger accounts described scenes of panic after the aircraft began its rapid descent. Israeli media published videos and photographs purporting to show injured passengers and the aftermath inside the aircraft, although some of the material could not be independently verified.
Israeli authorities said they would conduct a joint investigation into the incident and announced tighter security measures for airlines operating flights to Israel. Netanyahu praised the passengers and crew members who intervened, saying their actions helped prevent a potentially serious disaster.
The passengers later continued their journey to Israel aboard a replacement flydubai aircraft. Saudi Arabia’s handling of the emergency landing was particularly notable because the kingdom does not have formal diplomatic relations with Israel. Reuters later reported that Saudi Arabia declined an Israeli request to send military aircraft to retrieve the passengers.

sources.news_title: Omani Co-Pilot Tries to Crash Israel-Bound Flight After Stabbing Captain in Alleged Jihadist Terror Attack › American Greatness
sources.text:
A commercial jet traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv narrowly averted disaster Wednesday after the Omani co-pilot stabbed the captain with a pocket knife and attempted to crash the plane.
As Flydubai Flight 1073 approached Israel carrying 174–180 mostly Israeli passengers, it reportedly plummeted more than 14,000 feet in 30 seconds, 17,400 feet in less than two minutes, triggering a hijacking transponder code. Israel quickly scrambled fighter jets during the incident.
According to reports, the captain managed to open the release on the cockpit door as he lay bleeding on the floor, allowing passengers and crew to storm the cockpit and subdue the co-pilot as he was trying to sabotage the plane’s systems.
Two off-duty FlyDubai pilots onboard were able to land the Boeing 737 safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. Both pilots were injured and taken to hospital, while no passengers were reported seriously hurt. The attacker was arrested and interrogated by Saudi authorities.
The name of the co-pilot has not been released but he has been identified in media reports as an Omani national.
Israeli officials, speaking anonymously to Reuters and CNN, identified him as an Omani citizen who has worked for flydubai for a relatively short time—around nine months or less than a year.
Oman has no formal diplomatic relations with Israel and has officially rejected normalization.
Israeli authorities are examining how the Omani co-pilot was screened and assigned to a Tel Aviv-bound flight, and Transportation Minister Miri Regev ordered a review of flydubai’s crew practices on Israeli routes.
The captain has been identified in media reports as Indian national Smit Machchhar (also spelled Machchar), a former SpiceJet pilot who joined flydubai in 2022. Flydubai itself has not confirmed either pilot’s identity or nationality.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and security officials have characterized the incident as an attempted “jihadist terrorist attack,” rather than a mental-health episode, though the motive has not been publicly established.
“All passengers are out of harm’s way,” Netanyahu said in a video statement released by his office. He added that the quick thinking passengers and crew “saved many lives” and “prevented a heavy disaster.”
The prime minister also said he has ordered tighter security on both Israeli and non-Israeli carriers flying into Israel.
Hero passenger Yaniv Hayoun met with Netanyahu following the harrowing incident and described how he and other passengers stopped the attacker, saying that he put him in a chokehold and dragged him out of the cockpit before returning and grabbing the plane’s controls.
Hayoun described trying to get into the cockpit, where the stabbed pilot was up against the door making it hard to open at first.
Once he got in, Hayoun said he saw the attacker on the panel between the two seats.
“There were no pilots in the seats: one was on the floor, one was on the [panel],” Hayoun said, adding that he appeared to be trying to “disable the plane.”
“I called out to a bunch of Israelis on board, and two other guys came over. We pinned him down,” Hayoun said. “I jumped back, grabbed the controls, and started pulling back the handles.”
It all unfolded in seconds, he said.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said during a press conference Wednesday that there is no current threat against the United States.
“We take every incident like this very serious and we continue to look at the procedures that we have in place and continue to make sure the American people are safe,” Mullin told reporters.
He added that there were “no credible threats” to the United States and that an investigation into the incident was ongoing.

Jaw-Dropping Details Emerge From Hijacking Attempt On Israel-Bound Flight
sources.text:
Politics
Jaw-Dropping Details Emerge From Hijacking Attempt On Israel-Bound Flight
Harrowing new details have emerged from the midair chaos aboard a Flydubai flight bound for Israel, where officials say one pilot stabbed another and apparently tried to bring down the passenger jet before travelers rushed the cockpit and stopped him.
FlyDubai Flight 1073 was traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on Wednesday when a violent struggle erupted at the controls, sending the aircraft plunging thousands of feet and triggering emergency alerts before it diverted to Saudi Arabia.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said one pilot stabbed the other and “apparently attempted to crash the plane with its passengers on board,” nearly all of them Israelis.

sources.news_title: Wounded Flydubai Captain Opened Cockpit Door To Avert Disaster
sources.text:
Dramatic new details have surfaced regarding the harrowing moments aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073, revealing that the aircraft’s severely wounded captain managed to trigger the emergency cockpit door release while lying bleeding on the floor, allowing passengers to breach the flight deck and subdue the attacker. The heroic act, reported by Reuters citing security officials and eyewitness testimony, directly thwarted an apparent hijacking and suicide-dive attempt by the co-pilot over Saudi airspace.
The incident unfolded on Wednesday as the Boeing 737 MAX 8 was cruising en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv. According to Israeli defense sources, the co-pilot—formally identified by an Israeli official as an Omani national—produced an edged weapon inside the cockpit and launched a violent, unprovoked assault on the captain. After repeatedly stabbing the commanding pilot and leaving him critically injured on the floor, the assailant forced the aircraft’s flight controls into an aggressive downward angle, attempting to crash the airliner into the terrain below.
Aviation tracking telemetry revealed that the airliner pitched violently forward, “went into a spin,” and plunged more than 14,000 feet in just 30 seconds. As gravity shifted violently and sheer panic spread throughout the cabin, the wounded captain, despite losing significant amounts of blood, managed to stretch toward the electronic control console and hit the emergency latch release for the reinforced cockpit door. The quick action unlocked the secure barrier that typically prevents outside access during security emergencies.
Hearing shouting and feeling the uncontrolled plunge, a group of passengers—including several Israeli travelers—forced open the unlatched door and charged into the flight deck. Working alongside cabin crew members, the passengers overpowered the Omani co-pilot, wrestled the weapon away, and physically pinned him to the floor. Inside the cabin, medical professionals among the travelers immediately rendered emergency first aid to the captain to stem arterial bleeding.
Simultaneously, a catastrophic crash was averted thanks to the presence of a second set of Flydubai pilots who happened to be deadheading as passengers aboard the flight. The off-duty flight crew, who were scheduled to take over the aircraft for its subsequent operational rotation after touching down in Israel, rushed into the cockpit. The relief pilots took command of the controls, pulled the Boeing 737 out of its terminal spin, stabilized altitude, and coordinated an emergency approach into Tabuk Airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia.
Upon touching down in Tabuk, Saudi security units surrounded the airliner and detained the co-pilot, while emergency paramedics transported both the attacker and the captain to a local medical facility under heavy guard. While Israeli security agencies, alongside the Mossad and Shin Bet, are treating the assault as a deliberate act of terrorism, Flydubai emphasized that formal inquiries by civil aviation authorities remain ongoing to determine the attacker’s motives and background.
Following security clearances and high-level diplomatic coordination between Saudi, Emirati, and Israeli authorities, a replacement aircraft dispatched by Flydubai safely repatriated the 170 Israeli passengers and remaining travelers back to Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv late Wednesday evening, concluding one of the closest calls with aviation catastrophe in recent memory.
Wounded Flydubai Captain Opened Cockpit Door to Avert Disaster
The wounded captain of Flydubai flight FZ1073 managed to unlock the cockpit door from the floor while bleeding, enabling passengers and off-duty pilots to overpower a terrorist co-pilot and stop a 14,000-foot plunge.

sources.news_title: Smit Machchhar: The Indian-Origin Pilot Who Fought His Co-Pilot On A FlyDubai Flight FZ1073, Saving 180 Lives
sources.text:
Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian-origin pilot flying for FlyDubai, was stabbed in the cockpit of flight FZ1073 on Wednesday morning while en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv. His Omani co-pilot attacked him with a knife in an attempt to seize control of the aircraft. Despite his injuries, Machchhar fought back. Israeli passengers and additional crew members intervened, subdued the attacker, and helped bring the plane under control. The aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All approximately 180 people on board survived. A major disaster was averted because one captain refused to yield.
Machchhar is a Direct Entry Captain with FlyDubai who joined the airline in June 2022. Before that he spent nearly eleven years with the Indian carrier SpiceJet, rising to the role of Line Training Captain. He has logged approximately 9,750 flying hours, the great majority on Boeing 737 variants including the 737-800 and 737 MAX 8/9. More than 6,400 of those hours were as Pilot in Command. He is of Gujarati origin and holds a business administration degree. His professional background includes pilot mentoring and safety compliance.
The Attack In The Cockpit
Roughly two hours after departure from Dubai, while the Boeing 737 MAX 8 was over Jordanian airspace, the Omani co-pilot turned on Machchhar. He stabbed the captain and tried to force him from the controls. The aircraft plunged more than 14,000 feet in under thirty seconds. Emergency codes were transmitted, including the international signal for unlawful interference. Passengers heard screams from the front of the plane. The situation inside the cockpit was chaotic and bloody.
Machchhar, though wounded, resisted. His resistance bought critical seconds. Israeli passengers near the front forced their way toward the flight deck. Together with other crew members traveling on the flight, they pulled the co-pilot out and restrained him. An Israeli medical professional on board treated Machchhar’s stab wounds and worked to keep him conscious. Off-duty pilots among the passengers assisted in stabilizing the aircraft and guiding it to a safe landing.
The Attacker
The co-pilot has been identified in multiple reports as an Omani national who had been employed by flydubai for less than a year. His personal name has not been publicly released by authorities. Israeli officials are treating the incident as a suspected terrorist act. They have stated that the combination of the stabbing and the attempt to take control indicated an intent to crash the aircraft with everyone on board. The co-pilot is in Saudi custody and is being questioned. Investigators are examining his background, including questions about dual citizenship and how he came to be assigned to an Israel-bound flight.
Professional Skill Under Extreme Conditions
Machchhar’s extensive experience on the Boeing 737 family proved decisive. As Pilot in Command he retained final authority even while under physical assault. His ability to resist long enough for others to intervene, and the subsequent coordinated response by passengers and additional crew, prevented the aircraft from being lost. Flight data showed a dramatic and dangerous loss of altitude. The fact that the plane was recovered and landed intact is a direct result of that resistance and the rapid assistance that followed.
Both pilots were hospitalized in Saudi Arabia after the landing. Machchhar’s injuries were serious enough that he could not continue flying the aircraft himself. The successful outcome rested on the combination of his fight in the cockpit and the willingness of passengers, particularly Israelis on board, to act without hesitation.
A Narrow Margin
One hundred and eighty people boarded a routine commercial flight. One of the two men at the controls decided to turn the journey into a potential mass-casualty event. Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed yet continued to resist. Passengers and fellow crew members finished what he began. The plane is on the ground. Everyone is alive.
The investigation into the Omani co-pilot’s motives and background continues. What is already established is the sequence of events and the central role played by the Indian captain who refused to surrender the aircraft. In the confined space of a cockpit at altitude, with a knife in play and the plane diving, Smit Machchhar held the line long enough for help to arrive. That is the difference between catastrophe and survival.
